alignments.note: Anarthrous genitive; the case preposition *of* stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Article before νοῦν with no English determiner written; rule 23. Rule 13 forbids grouping it with its noun merely for convenience.
Accusative of respect; the supplied *in* realizes the case and stays with the noun, the article having no determiner to anchor it (rules 21, 23).
Rule 21: *of the* is one unit headed on *the*.
Participle rendered *supposing*; the complementizer *that* goes to the infinitival complement under rule 85.

Infinitive expanded into a finite clause; rule 85 gives the supplied complementizer *that* to the non-finite complement rather than to the governing verb, headed on the verb word *is*. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Article before εὐσέβειαν with no English determiner written; rule 23.

One Greek noun rendered *a way of gain*; rule 66 heads on *gain*, the word this corpus spends on πορισμός (cf. 6:6, where the bare noun is *gain*), *way* being the supplied generic completion and *a* its rule 7 determiner.

review_notes: Both articles are `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no determiner for either noun (rule 23); the supplied *in* and the phrase's own determiners stay where rules 21 and 51 put them.
The complementizer *that* is placed on εἶναι under rule 85 rather than on νομιζόντων.
